src: Laird, Iowa Legends (M.A. thesis, State University of Iowa, 1927; HathiTrust iau.31858060747148), pp. 89

Abbie Gardner Sharp, History of the Spirit Lake Massacre (1885), pp. 82-84 (same passage in the 1902 ed.; archive.org historyofspiritl00gardrich): places the cabin at Marble's Grove on the west side of the lake; no money mentioned
set.st: The Marble family, victims of the March 1857 Spirit Lake massacre, were said to have buried $1,500 in gold on their west-shore farm. It was never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis, from a letter via the Des Moines Register). Sharp's eyewitness history places the Marble cabin at Marble's Grove on the west side of the lake, says the raiders 'carried away what they wanted from Mr. Marble's place', and notes his stone-cutter's tools were later found in a hollow tree near the house; it says nothing of buried gold.

tw-ia-spirit-lake-marble-gold-1857.t: Sharp's eyewitness account says the raiders carried off what they wanted; the gold is a 1920s family tradition only.
